## PR Description

Closes #1614
### What changed

- One app-storage namespace (gh-1614 I1): new `AppStorage` resolver (`flutter_app/lib/apps/app_storage.dart`) is the single place resolving `apps/<id>/…` for listing (`AppsStore.listApps`), booting (`JsAppEngine`'s widget reader) and catalog installs (`installWidget`) — one validator, one clamp, no second path normalization.
- Listed ⇒ bootable (I2): `listApps` probes the boot entry through the same resolver; a listed app whose stored files are missing now renders the explicit "stored files missing" state naming the root and the exact path, instead of a tile that dies with `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` on tap.
- Honest failures (I3): entry-assembly failures name the storage root and every missing file; the widget-file reader clamps assembler paths (`jsr.include`, manifest `files`, imports) under the app dir, and traversal/absolute ids are rejected at list and read (AC4).

### Key decisions

- Shared pure resolver over a stateful facade (ticket open question 2): path math only, so VM/web/extension resolve identically.
- Two validation layers: strict `idPattern` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, the canonical new-id rule) plus an escape floor (`isResolvableId`) for ids already in user storage — legacy dirs like `bad_types` keep listing, while `../x`/absolute/separator ids never resolve.
- The manifest-declared `id` no longer overrides the storage dir name — a divergent declared id was itself a listed-unreadable vector (tile resolving a different root than storage).
- Reuses the #866 broken-app machinery (`JsAppInfo.error` badge + copyable dialog on every launch surface) — no new UI.

### How to verify

```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/app_storage_test.dart test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart test/apps/apps_store_test.dart test/apps/js_app_engine_test.dart
```

- AC1/AC3/AC4 + the root-resolution REG live in `test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart` (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`, torn-snapshot restore, hostile listings).
- Extension e2e (AC2) is not runnable in this environment (needs `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` + Chrome); the Dart-side IT pins the same listing + entry-assembly path the panel build executes — the `browser_ext/e2e` harness picks up the install-then-open journey when a bundled build exists.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD

  B[JsAppEngine boot reader] --> R
  I[installWidget writes] --> R
  R -->|valid id, clamped path| E[ExecutionEnv apps/<id>/…]
  R -->|traversal / absolute| X[rejected before any IO]
  L -->|entry missing| S[stored-files-missing state]

```

</details>

# gh-1614: [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')

## Description

## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

---

<details><summary>Original report (YuryBY, condensed)</summary>
Chrome extension: opening "2048 Мини 🎲" fails — `Bad state: app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js` (thrown from `JsAppEngine` when manifest/entry unreadable via the ExecutionEnv). Only `subscription-tracker` is bundled; user apps come from OPFS storage. Listing shows the app while reading fails → roots diverge. Reproduce, fix list/read divergence, make failure actionable, regression-test via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e.
</details>

## PR Description

Closes #1614
### What changed

- One app-storage namespace (gh-1614 I1): new `AppStorage` resolver (`flutter_app/lib/apps/app_storage.dart`) is the single place resolving `apps/<id>/…` for listing (`AppsStore.listApps`), booting (`JsAppEngine`'s widget reader) and catalog installs (`installWidget`) — one validator, one clamp, no second path normalization.
- Listed ⇒ bootable (I2): `listApps` probes the boot entry through the same resolver; a listed app whose stored files are missing now renders the explicit "stored files missing" state naming the root and the exact path, instead of a tile that dies with `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` on tap.
- Honest failures (I3): entry-assembly failures name the storage root and every missing file; the widget-file reader clamps assembler paths (`jsr.include`, manifest `files`, imports) under the app dir, and traversal/absolute ids are rejected at list and read (AC4).

### Key decisions

- Shared pure resolver over a stateful facade (ticket open question 2): path math only, so VM/web/extension resolve identically.
- Two validation layers: strict `idPattern` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, the canonical new-id rule) plus an escape floor (`isResolvableId`) for ids already in user storage — legacy dirs like `bad_types` keep listing, while `../x`/absolute/separator ids never resolve.
- The manifest-declared `id` no longer overrides the storage dir name — a divergent declared id was itself a listed-unreadable vector (tile resolving a different root than storage).
- Reuses the #866 broken-app machinery (`JsAppInfo.error` badge + copyable dialog on every launch surface) — no new UI.

### How to verify

```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/app_storage_test.dart test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart test/apps/apps_store_test.dart test/apps/js_app_engine_test.dart
```

- AC1/AC3/AC4 + the root-resolution REG live in `test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart` (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`, torn-snapshot restore, hostile listings).
- Extension e2e (AC2) is not runnable in this environment (needs `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` + Chrome); the Dart-side IT pins the same listing + entry-assembly path the panel build executes — the `browser_ext/e2e` harness picks up the install-then-open journey when a bundled build exists.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[AppsStore.listApps] --> R[AppStorage resolver]
  B[JsAppEngine boot reader] --> R
  I[installWidget writes] --> R
  R -->|valid id, clamped path| E[ExecutionEnv apps/<id>/…]
  R -->|traversal / absolute| X[rejected before any IO]
  L -->|entry missing| S[stored-files-missing state]
  B -->|entry missing| H[honest failure: root + missing paths]
```

</details>

# gh-1614: [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')

## Description

## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

---

<details><summary>Original report (YuryBY, condensed)</summary>
Chrome extension: opening "2048 Мини 🎲" fails — `Bad state: app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js` (thrown from `JsAppEngine` when manifest/entry unreadable via the ExecutionEnv). Only `subscription-tracker` is bundled; user apps come from OPFS storage. Listing shows the app while reading fails → roots diverge. Reproduce, fix list/read divergence, make failure actionable, regression-test via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e.
</details>

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1614` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +956
- **Deletions**: -24
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T22:14:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T22:42:48Z

## PR Description

Closes #1614
### What changed

- One app-storage namespace (gh-1614 I1): new `AppStorage` resolver (`flutter_app/lib/apps/app_storage.dart`) is the single place resolving `apps/<id>/…` for listing (`AppsStore.listApps`), booting (`JsAppEngine`'s widget reader) and catalog installs (`installWidget`) — one validator, one clamp, no second path normalization.
- Listed ⇒ bootable (I2): `listApps` probes the boot entry through the same resolver; a listed app whose stored files are missing now renders the explicit "stored files missing" state naming the root and the exact path, instead of a tile that dies with `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` on tap.
- Honest failures (I3): entry-assembly failures name the storage root and every missing file; the widget-file reader clamps assembler paths (`jsr.include`, manifest `files`, imports) under the app dir, and traversal/absolute ids are rejected at list and read (AC4).

### Key decisions

- Shared pure resolver over a stateful facade (ticket open question 2): path math only, so VM/web/extension resolve identically.
- Two validation layers: strict `idPattern` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, the canonical new-id rule) plus an escape floor (`isResolvableId`) for ids already in user storage — legacy dirs like `bad_types` keep listing, while `../x`/absolute/separator ids never resolve.
- The manifest-declared `id` no longer overrides the storage dir name — a divergent declared id was itself a listed-unreadable vector (tile resolving a different root than storage).
- Reuses the #866 broken-app machinery (`JsAppInfo.error` badge + copyable dialog on every launch surface) — no new UI.

### How to verify

```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/app_storage_test.dart test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart test/apps/apps_store_test.dart test/apps/js_app_engine_test.dart
```

- AC1/AC3/AC4 + the root-resolution REG live in `test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart` (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`, torn-snapshot restore, hostile listings).
- Extension e2e (AC2) is not runnable in this environment (needs `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` + Chrome); the Dart-side IT pins the same listing + entry-assembly path the panel build executes — the `browser_ext/e2e` harness picks up the install-then-open journey when a bundled build exists.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[AppsStore.listApps] --> R[AppStorage resolver]
  B[JsAppEngine boot reader] --> R
  I[installWidget writes] --> R
  R -->|valid id, clamped path| E[ExecutionEnv apps/<id>/…]
  R -->|traversal / absolute| X[rejected before any IO]
  L -->|entry missing| S[stored-files-missing state]
  B -->|entry missing| H[honest failure: root + missing paths]
```

</details>

# gh-1614: [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')

## Description

## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

---

<details><summary>Original report (YuryBY, condensed)</summary>
Chrome extension: opening "2048 Мини 🎲" fails — `Bad state: app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js` (thrown from `JsAppEngine` when manifest/entry unreadable via the ExecutionEnv). Only `subscription-tracker` is bundled; user apps come from OPFS storage. Listing shows the app while reading fails → roots diverge. Reproduce, fix list/read divergence, make failure actionable, regression-test via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e.
</details>

## PR Description

Closes #1614
### What changed

- One app-storage namespace (gh-1614 I1): new `AppStorage` resolver (`flutter_app/lib/apps/app_storage.dart`) is the single place resolving `apps/<id>/…` for listing (`AppsStore.listApps`), booting (`JsAppEngine`'s widget reader) and catalog installs (`installWidget`) — one validator, one clamp, no second path normalization.
- Listed ⇒ bootable (I2): `listApps` probes the boot entry through the same resolver; a listed app whose stored files are missing now renders the explicit "stored files missing" state naming the root and the exact path, instead of a tile that dies with `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` on tap.
- Honest failures (I3): entry-assembly failures name the storage root and every missing file; the widget-file reader clamps assembler paths (`jsr.include`, manifest `files`, imports) under the app dir, and traversal/absolute ids are rejected at list and read (AC4).

### Key decisions

- Shared pure resolver over a stateful facade (ticket open question 2): path math only, so VM/web/extension resolve identically.
- Two validation layers: strict `idPattern` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, the canonical new-id rule) plus an escape floor (`isResolvableId`) for ids already in user storage — legacy dirs like `bad_types` keep listing, while `../x`/absolute/separator ids never resolve.
- The manifest-declared `id` no longer overrides the storage dir name — a divergent declared id was itself a listed-unreadable vector (tile resolving a different root than storage).
- Reuses the #866 broken-app machinery (`JsAppInfo.error` badge + copyable dialog on every launch surface) — no new UI.

### How to verify

```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/app_storage_test.dart test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart test/apps/apps_store_test.dart test/apps/js_app_engine_test.dart
```

- AC1/AC3/AC4 + the root-resolution REG live in `test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart` (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`, torn-snapshot restore, hostile listings).
- Extension e2e (AC2) is not runnable in this environment (needs `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` + Chrome); the Dart-side IT pins the same listing + entry-assembly path the panel build executes — the `browser_ext/e2e` harness picks up the install-then-open journey when a bundled build exists.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[AppsStore.listApps] --> R[AppStorage resolver]
  B[JsAppEngine boot reader] --> R
  I[installWidget writes] --> R
  R -->|valid id, clamped path| E[ExecutionEnv apps/<id>/…]
  R -->|traversal / absolute| X[rejected before any IO]
  L -->|entry missing| S[stored-files-missing state]
  B -->|entry missing| H[honest failure: root + missing paths]
```

# gh-1614: [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')

## Description

## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

---

Only `subscription-tracker` is bundled; user apps come from OPFS storage. Listing shows the app while reading fails → roots diverge. Reproduce, fix list/read divergence, make failure actionable, regression-test via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e.

- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **Additions**: +956
- **Deletions**: -24

- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T22:42:48Z

## PR Description

Closes #1614
### What changed

- One app-storage namespace (gh-1614 I1): new `AppStorage` resolver (`flutter_app/lib/apps/app_storage.dart`) is the single place resolving `apps/<id>/…` for listing (`AppsStore.listApps`), booting (`JsAppEngine`'s widget reader) and catalog installs (`installWidget`) — one validator, one clamp, no second path normalization.
- Listed ⇒ bootable (I2): `listApps` probes the boot entry through the same resolver; a listed app whose stored files are missing now renders the explicit "stored files missing" state naming the root and the exact path, instead of a tile that dies with `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` on tap.
- Honest failures (I3): entry-assembly failures name the storage root and every missing file; the widget-file reader clamps assembler paths (`jsr.include`, manifest `files`, imports) under the app dir, and traversal/absolute ids are rejected at list and read (AC4).

### Key decisions

- Shared pure resolver over a stateful facade (ticket open question 2): path math only, so VM/web/extension resolve identically.
- Two validation layers: strict `idPattern` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, the canonical new-id rule) plus an escape floor (`isResolvableId`) for ids already in user storage — legacy dirs like `bad_types` keep listing, while `../x`/absolute/separator ids never resolve.
- The manifest-declared `id` no longer overrides the storage dir name — a divergent declared id was itself a listed-unreadable vector (tile resolving a different root than storage).
- Reuses the #866 broken-app machinery (`JsAppInfo.error` badge + copyable dialog on every launch surface) — no new UI.

### How to verify

```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/app_storage_test.dart test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart test/apps/apps_store_test.dart test/apps/js_app_engine_test.dart
```

- AC1/AC3/AC4 + the root-resolution REG live in `test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart` (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`, torn-snapshot restore, hostile listings).
- Extension e2e (AC2) is not runnable in this environment (needs `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` + Chrome); the Dart-side IT pins the same listing + entry-assembly path the panel build executes — the `browser_ext/e2e` harness picks up the install-then-open journey when a bundled build exists.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[AppsStore.listApps] --> R[AppStorage resolver]
  B[JsAppEngine boot reader] --> R
  I[installWidget writes] --> R
  R -->|valid id, clamped path| E[ExecutionEnv apps/<id>/…]
  R -->|traversal / absolute| X[rejected before any IO]
  L -->|entry missing| S[stored-files-missing state]
  B -->|entry missing| H[honest failure: root + missing paths]
```

blocks.text:
# gh-1614: [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')

## Description

## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

---

Chrome extension: opening "2048 Мини 🎲" fails — `Bad state: app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js` (thrown from `JsAppEngine` when manifest/entry unreadable via the ExecutionEnv). Only `subscription-tracker` is bundled; user apps come from OPFS storage. Listing shows the app while reading fails → roots diverge. Reproduce, fix list/read divergence, make failure actionable, regression-test via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e.
</details>

## PR Description

Closes #1614
### What changed

- One app-storage namespace (gh-1614 I1): new `AppStorage` resolver (`flutter_app/lib/apps/app_storage.dart`) is the single place resolving `apps/<id>/…` for listing (`AppsStore.listApps`), booting (`JsAppEngine`'s widget reader) and catalog installs (`installWidget`) — one validator, one clamp, no second path normalization.
- Listed ⇒ bootable (I2): `listApps` probes the boot entry through the same resolver; a listed app whose stored files are missing now renders the explicit "stored files missing" state naming the root and the exact path, instead of a tile that dies with `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` on tap.
- Honest failures (I3): entry-assembly failures name the storage root and every missing file; the widget-file reader clamps assembler paths (`jsr.include`, manifest `files`, imports) under the app dir, and traversal/absolute ids are rejected at list and read (AC4).

### Key decisions

- Shared pure resolver over a stateful facade (ticket open question 2): path math only, so VM/web/extension resolve identically.
- Two validation layers: strict `idPattern` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, the canonical new-id rule) plus an escape floor (`isResolvableId`) for ids already in user storage — legacy dirs like `bad_types` keep listing, while `../x`/absolute/separator ids never resolve.
- The manifest-declared `id` no longer overrides the storage dir name — a divergent declared id was itself a listed-unreadable vector (tile resolving a different root than storage).
- Reuses the #866 broken-app machinery (`JsAppInfo.error` badge + copyable dialog on every launch surface) — no new UI.

cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/app_storage_test.dart test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart test/apps/apps_store_test.dart test/apps/js_app_engine_test.dart

- AC1/AC3/AC4 + the root-resolution REG live in `test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart` (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`, torn-snapshot restore, hostile listings).
- Extension e2e (AC2) is not runnable in this environment (needs `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` + Chrome); the Dart-side IT pins the same listing + entry-assembly path the panel build executes — the `browser_ext/e2e` harness picks up the install-then-open journey when a bundled build exists.

blocks.text:
# gh-1614: [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')

## Description

## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals

blocks.text:
mount (`/project` → user-picked host dir; security-scoped bookmarks in
  `project_mount.json`; stale bookmark = "pick again" warning). Sessions on
  macOS are stored in the shared App Group container
  (`~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions`) so the Fa
  CLI and the sandboxed Fa macOS app see the same workspace-scoped sessions.
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/` — JS apps platform on `package:js_widget_runtime`
  (`^0.4.156` hosted — ships `jsr.openUrl` + the `webView` node and, since
  0.4.156 = upstream 9d57570 (gh-1341), the flutter_js bridge registers
  EVERY `__jsr_*` channel (`JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels` is the source
  of truth), so `jsr.hostCall`/`jsr.capture` no longer hang forever on JSC
  builds; the git pin convention is drop-the-override-once-hosted-lands;
  `js_app_engine.dart` wires `openUrlHandler` over `url_launcher`
  (LaunchMode.externalApplication, {'__error': ...} rejections) and passes a
  `JsWebViewHost` (fa_webview_host.dart, `flutter_inappwebview` over the
  system default data store — never incognito; iOS/Android/macOS only, other
  platforms get the renderer placeholder via `createFaWebViewHost`) to BOTH
  the JsRuntimeConfig and the JsonWidgetRenderer in js_app_view.dart —
  flutter_inappwebview rides the coherent 6.2.0-beta.3 set because 6.1.x's
  android impl evaluates getDefaultProguardFile('proguard-android.txt'),
  which AGP 9 removed (APK CI leg); the beta macos impl declares a 10.14
  floor while its Swift needs 10.15 (fails on both the SwiftPM and
  CocoaPods paths), so it is vendored with only the floor raised to the
  app's 14.0 (vendor/flutter_inappwebview_macos, pubspec override); return
  to ^6.1.x once 6.2.0 stable ships —
  earlier hosted line shipped the queued-callEvent-after-dispose guard +
  restart-safe bridge channels that the old git pin carried, plus the M3
  nodes/overlays/flChart/pickers/drawer catalog and M3 motion tokens; the
  use-after-free SIGSEGV is owned by `js_app_engine.dart`'s process-wide
  lifecycle serialization — releases must stay immediate, never deferred;
  the `map` node: center/zoom/markers/polylines/
  fitBounds, onTap/onMarkerTap). `flutter_js` itself is overridden in
  `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` to IstiN/flutter_js@74a11bf
  (fix-jscore-multi-instance: the shared native sendMessage callback routed
  to the LAST created runtime, so coexisting engines converted each other's
  JSValues with the wrong JSContext — SIGSEGV in JSC::JSLock::lock; the fork
  routes by executing context and refuses post-dispose evaluate): apps live in env-shared `apps/<id>/
  {manifest.json, widget.js}`; permissions in `apps_permissions.json` (network/
  allowedCommands/llm/homekit/health/contacts/calendar/microphone/
  notifications/media/keys/theme — default denied);
  `jsr.fa.*` bridge over exec (`fa.llm`, `fa.calendar`, `fa.home.*`,
  `fa.health.*`, `fa.asr.*`, `fa.notify.*`, `fa.theme` — declarative-only
  list/current/apply over installed theme packs, consent dialog per apply,
  no install/delete surface (issue #169); `fa.keys` — list/get/request the
  host's merged secrets (AgentService.hostSecrets); `request` renders the
  shared secret_request sheet from JsAppView and persists via
  AgentService.acceptSecretGrant; contacts is a gated "not
  available yet" stub); the `js-apps` skill is a package builtin
  (gh-1164 retired the `.fah/skills/` seeder — it is compiled into
  `builtinSkillFiles` by `scripts/gen_prompts.dart`, and the gh-1275
  packaging-content gate is `scripts/verify_builtin_skills.dart`, wired
  into the app build workflows). Bundled demos (seeded by
  `AppsStore.demoAppIds`, assets in `flutter_app/assets/apps/` — each id

Clean analyzer. Now the exhaustive pass. Let me re-examine specific concerns:

Actually since `withError` is new code duplicating the 14-field copy, a `copyWith({String? error})` would serve both. SUGGESTION.

3. **listApps: `missingEntry` probe adds one `exists` call per app per scan** — performance: an extra env round-trip per app per scan. The scan is already per-app multi-read (manifest read + i18n refs). One more small exists() is fine; but note it bypasses the cache: when entry missing, the fast path (cached parse) is skipped and the manifest is re-parsed every scan. That's intentional (heal detection). OK.

   Actually wait — subtle bug: when `missingEntry != null` and the app was CACHED and the manifest unchanged, the code re-parses (jsonDecode + i18n ref re-reads) — fine. But it also OVERWRITES `_manifestHashes[id]`/`_parsedApps[id]` with the same values. No bug.

   Another subtlety: the missing-entry state is NOT cached — every scan recomputes. Fine.

4. **`_missingEntryMessage` probes only `widget.js`** — apps with a live-tile entry (`tileWidget.entry` = e.g. 'widget_tile.js'): the tile boot path (`JsAppEngine.entryFile = tile entry`) requires manifest (widget.js exists probe) + tile entry file. If widget_tile.js is missing but widget.js exists, the tile lists CLEAN and tapping the tile → guardBrokenApp passes → assemble throws StateError → error card. Honest failure but not the missing-files state. SUGGESTION: probe `tileWidgetPath` too when `tileWidget != null`.

   Wait — actually check how the tile host boots. `JsAppEngine.entryFile` — where set? Let me check quickly. The engine constructor takes entryFile from app.tileWidgetPath presumably. Yes likely. This is a real (small) gap in I2 for tile apps. SUGGESTION.

5. **AC2 (extension e2e) not delivered** — PR honestly documents; ticket AC2 explicitly demands extension e2e. Note as gap in general review (ticket-context note per F10). Not blocking since the environment can't run it and the Dart IT covers the same path; but per F10 "note gaps in review" — I'll put it in the general comment + maybe an inline note? Inline comments must be on diff lines. The gap is a process gap, not a code line. General comment.

6. **`id` semantics change — permissions/install records keyed by dir name now**: `AppPermissionsStore` overrides keyed by `app.id` (dir name). Previously keyed by manifest-declared id when divergent. For all normal apps (manifest id == dir name) no change. Divergent legacy apps: permission grants orphaned → permissions revert to declared defaults (fail-closed). Also `.installed.json` keys are install ids (catalog ids) — dir names — unchanged. This behavior change deserves a mention (backward-compat dimension): acceptable, but worth noting in review as verified-safe.

7. **`removeWidget` still builds `apps/$appId` raw** — appId comes from listed apps (resolvable) or catalog entry.id. But `apps_catalog_tool.dart:201 removeWidget(id)` — id from the model/tool args! An agent calling `remove_app` with a hostile id `'../evil'` would `listDir('apps/../evil')` and `remove('apps/../evil/...')` — path traversal DELETE outside the namespace! Wait — check apps_catalog_tool to see if id is validated. This is pre-existing (not introduced by the diff), but the PR's stated invariant is "an id arriving from user storage can never escape the namespace" — the removal tool is part of the catalog lifecycle the PR touched (installWidget migrated, removeWidget NOT). An agent-facing tool accepting arbitrary ids → `removeWidget('../x')` → `_env.remove('apps/../x/...')` → could delete `apps/` contents or outside... Actually `remove('apps/../evil/name', recursive: true)` → path 'evil/name' relative to env root — deletes arbitrary env files! Hmm wait: `_readInstalled()` first; `force: false` → `!meta.containsKey(appId)` → returns false unless the install record contains '../evil' — records keyed by install id; an agent can't forge .installed.json... but it can write .installed.json via file tools? The agent has full env file access anyway (it can rm anything directly!). The Fa agent can already touch any env file with its file tools — so traversal in the tool is no privilege escalation for the agent. It's a defense-in-depth gap, not a vuln. Out-of-diff finding → general review, SUGGESTION (consistency: removeWidget/resetToFactory/_seedDemoApp should also route through AppStorage). Since the PR claims "one namespace, no second path normalization", the incomplete migration is worth an IMPORTANT? It's not a correctness bug in what shipped (catalog ids are validated canonical at install; installWidget now rejects hostile names). The remaining raw sites are internal flows with controlled ids (seedDemoIds = const [] now; removeWidget takes catalog/tool ids). I'll rate IMPORTANT (real maintainability debt within the PR's own stated invariant) — actually, per verdict rules: IMPORTANT = "real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR works as shipped". Yes, IMPORTANT.

8. **`installWidget` charset tightening** — `AppStorage.appFile` rejects any archive entry with chars outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` per segment (also caps 128/segment). Previously any name wrote. A legit published catalog widget with, say, `assets/My Icon.svg` or a Cyrillic-named i18n ref file would now FAIL install with ArgumentError (surfaced as install-failed snack). mount (`/project` → user-picked host dir; security-scoped bookmarks in
  `project_mount.json`; stale bookmark = "pick again" warning). Sessions on
  macOS are stored in the shared App Group container
  (`~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions`) so the Fa
  CLI and the sandboxed Fa macOS app see the same workspace-scoped sessions.
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/` — JS apps platform on `package:js_widget_runtime`
  (`^0.4.156` hosted — ships `jsr.openUrl` + the `webView` node and, since
  0.4.156 = upstream 9d57570 (gh-1341), the flutter_js bridge registers
  EVERY `__jsr_*` channel (`JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels` is the source
  of truth), so `jsr.hostCall`/`jsr.capture` no longer hang forever on JSC
  builds; the git pin convention is drop-the-override-once-hosted-lands;
  `js_app_engine.dart` wires `openUrlHandler` over `url_launcher`
  (LaunchMode.externalApplication, {'__error': ...} rejections) and passes a
  `JsWebViewHost` (fa_webview_host.dart, `flutter_inappwebview` over the
  system default data store — never incognito; iOS/Android/macOS only, other
  platforms get the renderer placeholder via `createFaWebViewHost`) to BOTH
  the JsRuntimeConfig and the JsonWidgetRenderer in js_app_view.dart —
  flutter_inappwebview rides the coherent 6.2.0-beta.3 set because 6.1.x's
  android impl evaluates getDefaultProguardFile('proguard-android.txt'),
  which AGP 9 removed (APK CI leg); the beta macos impl declares a 10.14
  floor while its Swift needs 10.15 (fails on both the SwiftPM and
  CocoaPods paths), so it is vendored with only the floor raised to the
  app's 14.0 (vendor/flutter_inappwebview_macos, pubspec override); return
  to ^6.1.x once 6.2.0 stable ships —
  earlier hosted line shipped the queued-callEvent-after-dispose guard +
  restart-safe bridge channels that the old git pin carried, plus the M3
  nodes/overlays/flChart/pickers/drawer catalog and M3 motion tokens; the
  use-after-free SIGSEGV is owned by `js_app_engine.dart`'s process-wide
  lifecycle serialization — releases must stay immediate, never deferred;
  the `map` node: center/zoom/markers/polylines/
  fitBounds, onTap/onMarkerTap). `flutter_js` itself is overridden in
  `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` to IstiN/flutter_js@74a11bf
  (fix-jscore-multi-instance: the shared native sendMessage callback routed
  to the LAST created runtime, so coexisting engines converted each other's
  JSValues with the wrong JSContext — SIGSEGV in JSC::JSLock::lock; the fork
  routes by executing context and refuses post-dispose evaluate): apps live in env-shared `apps/<id>/
  {manifest.json, widget.js}`; permissions in `apps_permissions.json` (network/
  allowedCommands/llm/homekit/health/contacts/calendar/microphone/
  notifications/media/keys/theme — default denied);
  `jsr.fa.*` bridge over exec (`fa.llm`, `fa.calendar`, `fa.home.*`,
  `fa.health.*`, `fa.asr.*`, `fa.notify.*`, `fa.theme` — declarative-only
  list/current/apply over installed theme packs, consent dialog per apply,
  no install/delete surface (issue #169); `fa.keys` — list/get/request the
  host's merged secrets (AgentService.hostSecrets); `request` renders the
  shared secret_request sheet from JsAppView and persists via
  AgentService.acceptSecretGrant; contacts is a gated "not
  available yet" stub); the `js-apps` skill is a package builtin
  (gh-1164 retired the `.fah/skills/` seeder — it is compiled into
  `builtinSkillFiles` by `scripts/gen_prompts.dart`, and the gh-1275
  packaging-content gate is `scripts/verify_builtin_skills.dart`, wired
  into the app build workflows). Bundled demos (seeded by
  `AppsStore.demoAppIds`, assets in `flutter_app/assets/apps/` — each id
  MUST also have its `- assets/apps/<id>/` entry in pubspec.yaml, gated by
  `test/apps/demo_assets_declared_test.dart`): calculator,
  weather, stocks, crypto, animation-showcase, yolo-hello, calendar
  (`jsr.fa.calendar`), map (`map` node), health + homekit (real bridge on
  iOS, honest demo-panel fallback elsewhere), fitness-trainer — guided
  workout with a 3D animated coach (a realistic human baked from NAVER's
  anny body model — Apache-2.0 — into
  `assets/apps/fitness-trainer/models/coach_anny.glb` with 10
  hand-authored skeletal clips; baker script in
  `references/anny/tools/bake_coach_glb.py` — anny `local-bone` deltas in
  world axes → glTF: IBMs are column-major, mesh split into ≤16-joint
  surfaces for flame_3d, and the skinned node must NOT be parented to a
  joint (flame_3d's dependency count then never settles); rendered via
  the `scene3d` node + flame_3d; START-driven exercise/rest steps with
  per-clip mapping, pause/skip/quit, sessions persisted via jsr.storage;
  `integration_test/fitness_coach_screenshot_test.dart` screenshot-verifies
  it on the macOS host), english-teacher — the "Language Tutor": Duolingo-style
  quiz sessions (hearts/XP/streak, choice + typing modes), a per-language
  offline word bank (en/de/es/fr/pl picker persisted via jsr.storage),
  LLM-generated extra words via `jsr.fa.llm.chat` (manifest `llm: true`),
  3d-game (`scene3d` node +
  `jsr.scene3d.*` bridge on the runtime's flutter_cube/flame_3d dispatcher
  — the engine's `JsRuntimeConfig` and both renderers (JsAppView,
  AppTileHost) wire `js3dHost: createJs3dHost()`, tap picking flows back
  via `dispatchHostEvent('scene3d.tap:<id>')`). Demo seeding is
  ownership-aware: `apps/.demo_seeds.json` records sha256 of each file as
  last seeded — a file whose content no longer matches is user/agent-owned
  and never overwritten, UNLESS the on-disk manifest is unparseable (a
  half-written skeleton is re-seeded, not protected: it bricks the tile), (`resetDemoApp(id)` force-restores the reference
  version, `storage.json` untouched). A demo id whose seeding FAILS
  (missing/corrupt asset) never kills the rest: it lands in
  `AppsStore.failedSeeds` (id → error text) and gets an error badge on its
  launcher tile; tapping the tile shows a dialog with the copyable error
  (hand it to Fa for a fix). `open_app_tool.dart` registers
  the agent tool `open_app`
  (host callback navigates via `js_app_navigation.dart` `pushJsApp`).

  (`{entry: 'widget_tile.js', size: 'WxH', refreshSeconds?}` →
  `JsAppInfo.tileWidget`; size in icon-slot cells, W 1–4 × H 1–4, default

content.thinking:
More unchanged raw-path functions confirmed (`isEmptyAppDir`, `isCleanInstall`, `missingInstalledFiles` — note `missingInstalledFiles` is exactly the torn-snapshot detector for issue #201; interesting: the auto-update healer path (catalog_auto_update) probably re-installs when files are missing — the PR's missingEntry state would be healed by that existing machinery. Good design coherence.)

Now let me find the exact line numbers in the diff for inline comments. The rule: inline comment lines must exist in the PR diff (added lines). Let me get the diff with line numbers of the new file and changed hunks.

Plan of inline comments:

1. **apps_store.dart — missingEntry probe / tile entry gap (SUGGESTION)** — line where `final missingEntry =` is. Need the new-file line number in the PR head branch.

2. **apps_store.dart — `_validateI18nRefs` appFile throw asymmetry (SUGGESTION)** — the `AppStorage.appFile(id, ref)` line.

3. **apps_store.dart — `withError` 14-field copy duplication (SUGGESTION)**.

4. **app_storage.dart — isResolvableId allows embedded dots/mid-dots, spaces, unicode — intentional per design (legacy floor); no comment needed. Instead: comment about `_missingEntryMessage`/probe being main-entry only? That duplicates #1. Pick different: app_storage.dart `isValidRelativePath` ASCII-only charset vs normalizeRefPath asymmetry — that's the same theme as #2. Put the charset note on `_segmentPattern` line in app_storage.dart (in diff), and keep #2 on the _validateI18nRefs line? Two comments one theme — better single comment at _validateI18nRefs (the behavior change site) mentioning the read-side symmetry. I'll keep one.

5. **app_storage_test.dart — 'Party-Time' fixture clarity (SUGGESTION)** — hmm, that test line is in app_namespace_it_test.dart (_HostileListEnv). Line: the `FileInfo(name: 'Party-Time', ...)` in the test's hostile const. In diff (new file). SUGGESTION.

Wait — reconsider #5: is 'Party-Time' actually skipped due to missing manifest? The fixture writes manifest only for apps/ok. _HostileListEnv injects '../evil', 'Party-Time', '/abs' — none have manifests. So all three are excluded: two by the id gate, one by missing manifest. Test asserts only ['ok']. It passes. The test's intent (hostile names never listed) is verified for '../evil' and '/abs'; 'Party-Time' is mislabeled as hostile (it's a legit legacy-shaped id per the two-layer design). The cleaner fixture: give 'Party-Time' a manifest+entry and expect it LISTED (pinning the legacy floor), or drop it. That's a decent suggestion-level test-clarity comment.

6. **js_app_engine.dart — `_clamp` correctness**: any real issue? Let me think once more about `_clamp` with `dir` = '.widgets/s-1/w' style (dirOverride). prefix '.widgets/s-1/w/'. Path '.widgets/s-1/widget.js' → fine. Windows backslashes in dirOverride? isSafeDir allows interior backslashes?? isSafeDir checks startsWith('\\') only, and splits on '/' — a dir 'a\\b' (single segment with backslash) PASSES isSafeDir! Then _clamp replaces '\\' with '/' → dir 'a/b' semantics vs prefix computed from original dir 'a\\b/' — normalized paths never match the raw-backslash prefix → EVERYTHING refused → reader answers missing → honest boot failure (not escape). dirOverride for dynamic widgets derives from session paths encoded with dashes (no backslashes: `--Users-My Projects-x--`). Fine — no finding; the doc comment even explains the design.

   Edge in _clamp: `normalized == dir` returns dir — for dir '.' would... isSafeDir rejects. OK.

7. **js_app_engine.dart — `_bootFailure`**: uses raw `'$dir/${AppStorage.manifestFile}'` — could use AppStorage.appFile(dir-as-id)? No — dir isn't an id. Fine as-is (dir pre-validated by isSafeDir). No finding.

8. **Test for installWidget hostile names** — no test. Fold into general? I'll add to comment #2's file (install-path note) — actually cleaner: keep #2 comment focused; add test-coverage sentence there.

Also double-check: does anything else call `JsAppInfo.fromManifest` with fallbackId that ISN'T a dir name? grep tests: app_storage_test REG uses fallbackId '2048' literal. apps_store uses dir entry.name. Bundled demo flow? `_seedDemoApp` doesn't build JsAppInfo. app_launcher `_fallbackApp` direct ctor. OK.

One more correctness scenario — **`withError` on the CACHED path**: when entry missing but cached healthy parse exists AND manifest unchanged AND i18n unchanged — wait, the cache gate has `missingEntry == null` so missing-entry never takes the cached branch. ✓.

**Heal race**: entry restored between probe and cached-branch — benign.

**`_parsedApps` caching withError copy?** No — listed copy only. ✓ (comment in code explains).

**Sort order**: apps sorted by name; missing-files apps keep name. ✓.

**i18n refusal log**: `AppLog.i('apps', 'i18n ref ${app.dir}/$path refused — skipped')` — app.dir could THROW for unresolvable id? id is resolvable (listed) — ✓ safe.

Now — is there anything BLOCKING? Let me scan the test-only change in apps_store_test once more: adds widget.js so the tiles aren't flagged... the test at line ~801 asserts error badge on 'bad_types' due to `"allowedCommands": 5` (invalid manifest) — with entry now present, the manifest error still flags. ✓ consistent.

And widgets_catalog_sheet_test focus-timer: adds widget.js so the Update button (not broken state) shows. ✓.

CI status: no ci_failures.md input → CI presumably green; machine job dev ✅ per ticket.md.

Severity summary:
- BLOCKING: 0
- IMPORTANT: 1 (general-only: incomplete namespace migration — removeWidget/isCleanInstall/missingInstalledFiles/_seedDemoApp raw paths + unvalidated agent-supplied id into removeWidget) — hmm, IMPORTANT but general-comment-only (unchanged code). That's allowed: "Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in outputs/pr_review_general.md".

Actually wait — should the incomplete-migration finding be IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION? The PR works as shipped; the claim "one namespace, no second path normalization" is about list/boot/install and those ARE unified. The remaining raw sites are mostly internal with controlled ids. The one externally-fed site (catalog tool remove id) crosses no trust boundary the agent doesn't already have. I'll rate it IMPORTANT (it's exactly the kind of debt the ticket's I1 wanted eliminated; next person will assume it's done).

Verdict: no BLOCKING → `APPROVE` per verdict rules.

issueCounts: blocking 0, important 1, suggestions: let me count: 
- S1 tile-entry probe gap (inline, apps_store.dart)
- S2 i18n ref charset asymmetry install vs read (inline, apps_store.dart _validateI18nRefs)

issueCounts format from few-shot: {"blocking":1,"important":1,"suggestions":1} — counts. blocking:0, important:1, suggestions:4.

Wait — verdict mapping: no BLOCKING → APPROVE even with IMPORTANT. ✓ "APPROVE with remaining ⚠️/💡 findings is the expected terminal state". But hold on — is the IMPORTANT general finding "real maintainability debt worth fixing" without blocking? Yes, and APPROVE is correct per the machine protocol.

Hmm, let me reconsider whether the tile-entry probe gap should be IMPORTANT instead of SUGGESTION. Ticket I2: "anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit 'stored files missing' state". For a tile-widget app, which "entry"? The ticket's defect is app boot. The tile entry is part of the app's surface. A listed tile app with missing tile entry → tile render fails with honest error card (via #866 machinery — actually does the tile host render an error card? AppTileHost shows... let me not over-verify; the engine's start error path is handled and logged). The main open-app boot works. I'll keep SUGGESTION but phrase the user impact precisely.

blocks.text:
mount (`/project` → user-picked host dir; security-scoped bookmarks in
  `project_mount.json`; stale bookmark = "pick again" warning). Sessions on
  macOS are stored in the shared App Group container
  (`~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions`) so the Fa
  CLI and the sandboxed Fa macOS app see the same workspace-scoped sessions.
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/` — JS apps platform on `package:js_widget_runtime`
  (`^0.4.156` hosted — ships `jsr.openUrl` + the `webView` node and, since
  0.4.156 = upstream 9d57570 (gh-1341), the flutter_js bridge registers
  EVERY `__jsr_*` channel (`JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels` is the source
  of truth), so `jsr.hostCall`/`jsr.capture` no longer hang forever on JSC
  builds; the git pin convention is drop-the-override-once-hosted-lands;
  `js_app_engine.dart` wires `openUrlHandler` over `url_launcher`
  (LaunchMode.externalApplication, {'__error': ...} rejections) and passes a
  `JsWebViewHost` (fa_webview_host.dart, `flutter_inappwebview` over the
  system default data store — never incognito; iOS/Android/macOS only, other
  platforms get the renderer placeholder via `createFaWebViewHost`) to BOTH
  the JsRuntimeConfig and the JsonWidgetRenderer in js_app_view.dart —
  flutter_inappwebview rides the coherent 6.2.0-beta.3 set because 6.1.x's
  android impl evaluates getDefaultProguardFile('proguard-android.txt'),
  which AGP 9 removed (APK CI leg); the beta macos impl declares a 10.14
  floor while its Swift needs 10.15 (fails on both the SwiftPM and
  CocoaPods paths), so it is vendored with only the floor raised to the
  app's 14.0 (vendor/flutter_inappwebview_macos, pubspec override); return
  to ^6.1.x once 6.2.0 stable ships —
  earlier hosted line shipped the queued-callEvent-after-dispose guard +
  restart-safe bridge channels that the old git pin carried, plus the M3
  nodes/overlays/flChart/pickers/drawer catalog and M3 motion tokens; the
  use-after-free SIGSEGV is owned by `js_app_engine.dart`'s process-wide
  lifecycle serialization — releases must stay immediate, never deferred;
  the `map` node: center/zoom/markers/polylines/
  fitBounds, onTap/onMarkerTap). `flutter_js` itself is overridden in
  `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` to IstiN/flutter_js@74a11bf
  (fix-jscore-multi-instance: the shared native sendMessage callback routed
  to the LAST created runtime, so coexisting engines converted each other's
  JSValues with the wrong JSContext — SIGSEGV in JSC::JSLock::lock; the fork
  routes by executing context and refuses post-dispose evaluate): apps live in env-shared `apps/<id>/
  {manifest.json, widget.js}`; permissions in `apps_permissions.json` (network/
  allowedCommands/llm/homekit/health/contacts/calendar/microphone/
  notifications/media/keys/theme — default denied);
  `jsr.fa.*` bridge over exec (`fa.llm`, `fa.calendar`, `fa.home.*`,
  `fa.health.*`, `fa.asr.*`, `fa.notify.*`, `fa.theme` — declarative-only
  list/current/apply over installed theme packs, consent dialog per apply,
  no install/delete surface (issue #169); `fa.keys` — list/get/request the
  host's merged secrets (AgentService.hostSecrets); `request` renders the
  shared secret_request sheet from JsAppView and persists via
  AgentService.acceptSecretGrant; contacts is a gated "not
